title: Poisson-Process Topic Model for Integrating Knowledge from Pre-trained Language Models
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
subcategory: embedding-space topic model with statistical guarantees
task: Topic estimation from contextual word embeddings
problem: Count-based topic models ignore word context; embedding-based neural models lack theoretical guarantees and require bespoke architectures.
architecture: PPTM: each document is a sequence of contextual word embeddings modelled as a Poisson point process whose intensity is a convex combination of K topic densities. TRACE estimator: UMAP reduction, net-rounding (k-means hyperwords forming a Voronoi partition), any count-based topic model as plug-in (default Topic-SCORE with SPA vertex hunting), then kernel smoothing back to continuous topic densities.
llm_or_encoder: BERT contextual word embeddings (flair library); LLM treated as a black box, no fine-tuning

datasets.name: Associated Press
datasets.details: 2246 news articles, 2106 kept after removing articles under 50 words

datasets.name: MADStat
datasets.details: abstracts of 83,331 statistics papers (36 journals, 1975-2015); 50,837 after removing abstracts under 38 words

metrics: convergence rate and minimax lower bound (theory)
key_results: Theory: rate of convergence for beta-Holder topic densities that matches the minimax lower bound when beta <= 1.
TRACE has the best TC in most settings (e.g. AP, K = 5: 0.528 vs ECRTM 0.477 and FASTopic 0.411); FASTopic is best on plain TD, TRACE on Embedded TD.
MADStat clustering accuracy: journal 0.275 vs 0.256 (ECRTM) and 0.254 (FASTopic); author pairs 0.617 vs 0.589 and 0.600.
strengths: Model-agnostic: any classical topic model can be plugged in without changes.
Gives context-dependent topic relevance for each word occurrence (e.g. 'bond' in finance vs other contexts) with a formal guarantee.

limitations.text: Contextual embeddings greatly increase computation, especially for long documents; hyperword binning loses information and M must be tuned (bias-variance trade-off).
Real-data evaluation uses two corpora and two neural baselines; ECRTM has higher TC on AP at K = 50.

notes: Authors suggest sentence-level 'hyper-sentences' as future work.
